title: Minimum Increment Operations to Make Array Beautiful
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n and an integer k, determine the least number of increment operations required to ensure every subarray of size 3 or more has a maximum element of at least k.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n and an integer k, determine the least number of increment operations required to ensure every subarray of size 3 or more has a maximum element of at least k. An increment operation increases an element at any index by 1.
constraints: Incrementing one element by one costs one operation.
Make every contiguous subarray of length at least three contain a value at least k; return minimum cost.
hints: It is enough to ensure every length-three window contains a qualifying position.
Track the minimum cost when the latest chosen/qualified position is one, two, or three steps back.
Shift three costs; the new chosen cost is min(states)+max(0,k-value).
A gap of three unqualified positions is forbidden, so these three states describe every feasible prefix.
editorial: A gap of three unqualified positions is forbidden, so these three states describe every feasible prefix.

tests.explanation: Raising selected positions to four costs three and covers every length-three window.
Choosing the two final positions costs four, which is minimum.
